To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) low-excitation FRII radio galaxies are generally X-ray faint; 2) low-excitation radio galaxies have systematically lower X-ray nuclear fluxes and higher X-ray absorption than narrow-line radio galaxies of similar radio power; 3) low-excitation and high-excitation radio galaxies show no evidence for a difference in their X-ray spectral shapes; 4) low-excitation sources are generally fainter in the mid-infrared than high-excitation sources of similar radio power.
